requirements.text: If the lamp ESA is type-approved under R10, approval may be as a component (fitted to any vehicle type) or as a separate technical unit (for specific vehicle type(s) requested by the ESA manufacturer).
The representative ESA system must fulfil the requirements of paragraph 6 and, if applicable, paragraph 7 of R10 for type approval to be granted.
The ESA approval is documented using the communication form modelled in Annex 3B.

Notification of approval or refusal of the ESA type uses the Annex 3B form. The applicant supplies photographs and/or diagrams or drawings on an appropriate scale, in a format not larger than A4 (210 x 297 mm) or folded to those dimensions.
The ESA (rear lamp with LED electronics) must be designed, constructed and fitted so that, in normal conditions of use, it complies with the requirements of UN R10.
The ESA (rear lamp) must be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.

Before testing, the Technical Service and the manufacturer must prepare a test plan. At minimum it covers mode of operation, stimulated functions, monitored functions, pass/fail criteria and intended emissions.

When measured by the Annex 7 method, broadband emissions of the ESA must stay within the limits. These are 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m at 30-75 MHz (decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m at 75-400 MHz (increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz) and a constant 63 dB microvolts/m at 400-1,000 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.
On the ESA representative of its type, measured broadband values in dB microvolts/m must be below the type approval limits.
Electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type must be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

When measured by the Annex 8 method, narrowband emissions must stay within the limits. These are 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m at 30-75 MHz (decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m at 75-400 MHz (increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz) and a constant 53 dB microvolts/m at 400-1,000 MHz, as shown in Appendix 7.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value in dB microvolts/m must be below the type approval limits.
The emission of the ESA representative of its type must be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2, as described in Annex 10, for the levels in Table 1.
Transient pulse amplitudes must not exceed +75 V / -100 V for 12 V systems, or +150 V / -450 V for 24 V systems.
Test the radiated electromagnetic immunity of the representative ESA by a method chosen from those in Annex 9.
Test the ESA's radiated immunity by the Annex 9 method(s). Apply the Table 2a severity over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band. Apply the Table 2b minimum test level over the whole band.
During the Annex 9 tests there must be no degradation of performance of the immunity related functions, such as stop lamp and rear position lamp operation.

Test ESA immunity to supply-line transients per Annex 10 (ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b; ISO 16750-2 starting profile where applicable). Use the Table 3a and 3b levels and functional status classes.
Measure broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA. Unless Annex 7 states otherwise, perform the test according to CISPR 25.
Test the ESA in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load. The REESS and charging conditions apply only to ESAs in grid-coupled REESS charging mode.
For an ESA not involved in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid, perform the test by the ALSE method in clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
If an open area test site (OATS) is used instead of an ALSE for the radiated broadband emission measurement, it must comply with CISPR 16-1-4.

Take ambient measurements before or after the main test. Extraneous noise or signal must be at least 6 dB below the interference limits of paragraph 6.5.2.1, except for intentional narrowband ambient transmissions.
Broadband emission limits apply throughout 30 to 1,000 MHz for ESA measurements in an ALSE or OATS.
Measure with a quasi-peak or peak detector. The limits are quasi-peak limits, so apply a 20 dB correction factor (per CISPR 12) if peak detectors are used.

Perform the measurements with a spectrum analyser or scanning receiver using the Table 1 and Table 2 parameters. FFT-based instruments must meet CISPR 16-1-1, record continuously, and use at least 1 s per analysis band.
When a spectrum analyser is used, use the Table 1 parameters for 30 to 1,000 MHz. For peak detection the video bandwidth must be at least three times the RBW.
When a scanning receiver is used, use the Table 2 parameters for 30 to 1,000 MHz: 120 kHz bandwidth, 60 kHz maximum step, and minimum dwell of 5 ms (peak) or 1 s (quasi-peak).

Test the configuration with the LV harness closer to the antenna, unless otherwise specified. Perform the test at the CISPR 12 intervals across 30 to 1,000 MHz, or use the 14-band alternative with accredited laboratory data.
Take the maximum reading relative to the limit (horizontal/vertical polarization) in each of the 14 frequency bands as the characteristic reading.

Demonstrate radiated immunity using any combination of the listed test methods (ISO 11452-2, -3, -4, -5, -11), chosen at the manufacturer's discretion, provided the combination covers the full frequency range in Annex 9 para 3.1. The REESS-charging combination does not apply to this lamp.
Radiated immunity test conditions for the ESA must be according to ISO 11452-1.
The ESA under test must be switched on and stimulated into normal operation. It must be arranged as defined in Annex 9 unless individual test methods dictate otherwise.
Extraneous equipment needed to operate the ESA must not be in place during calibration. None may be closer than 1 m from the reference point during calibration.
The test signal generating equipment and its layout must have the same specification as used during each appropriate calibration phase.

Test over 20 to 6,000 MHz with steps per ISO 11452-1. Use AM (1 kHz, 80% depth) at 20–400 MHz, PM2 (Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs) at 2,700–3,100 MHz, and PM3 (Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs) at 380–2,700 MHz and 3,100–6,000 MHz. Different settings apply only if agreed between Technical Service and manufacturer.

The Technical Service must test at the ISO 11452-1 intervals across 20 to 6,000 MHz. Alternatively, it may use reduced spot frequencies if the manufacturer supplies whole-band measurement data from an ISO 17025 accredited laboratory recognised by the Type Approval Authority.
If the ESA fails the Annex 9 tests, the failure must be verified as occurring under the relevant test conditions and not as a result of uncontrolled fields.
When tested in an absorber chamber, establish the test field using the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2, and perform the test with vertical polarization.
If the TEM-cell method is used, perform the test according to ISO 11452-3. The Technical Service chooses maximum field coupling to the ESA or to the wiring harness inside the TEM cell.

If the BCI method is used, test according to ISO 11452-4 on a test bench. Use the substitution method with the probe 150 mm from the ESA, or the closed-loop method with the probe 900 mm from the ESA. Alternatively, test the ESA installed in the vehicle per ISO 11451-4 using the substitution method with the probe 150 mm from the ESA.
If BCI is used, place all harnesses on a non-conductive, low-permittivity material (εr≤1.4) at (50 ± 5) mm above the ground plane.
If BCI is used, unless otherwise specified, connect the ESA case to the ground plane either directly or via a defined impedance.

Apply ISO 7637-2 test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, and the ISO 16750-2 starting profile, to the supply lines and any other connections of the ESA that may be operationally connected to supply lines. The starting profile does not apply to ESAs reserved exclusively for electric vehicles.
Measure transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA on its supply lines, and on other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines, according to ISO 7637-2.
The lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) fall within the scope of UN R148 and must meet its requirements.
The type approval application must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by their duly accredited representative.

Provide drawings detailed enough to identify the lamp type and category. They must show the mounting position(s), the reference axis and centre, the apparent surface limits of the functions, the approval marking space, and any other items listed (source modules, interdependent lamps, vehicle manufacturer logo) where applicable.

Provide a brief technical description covering, where applicable, the light source category or module identification code, any control gear or variable intensity control not part of the lamp, LED substitute source categories, rear window optical properties for devices mounted inside the vehicle, and the vehicle manufacturer logo statement.
Unless otherwise specified for the relevant lamp, submit two complete samples of the lamp. Symmetrical left/right lamps may be submitted as two identical samples suitable for one side only.
A separate approval is required for each lamp function listed in paragraph 1 (here position, stop and reversing).

Approval of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps may be granted only if each lamp meets this Regulation or another Regulation. Lamps that meet none of them shall not be part of the unit.

The lamp type submitted must meet the requirements of this Regulation for approval to be granted. If the lamps form an interdependent system, all of its devices must be submitted by the same applicant.

Each approved lamp type must have an approval number recorded in the Annex 1 communication form. The same number may cover a device or system incorporating several lamps, but not another type of lamp of the same function.
The symbols identifying each light-signalling lamp function for which type approval was granted must be applied, using the symbols in Table 1.
Mark the functions approved with the Table 1 symbols: rear position lamp R1 or R2, stop lamp S1 or S2, reversing lamp AR, according to the function and type, steady or variable.
Use the applicable change index for each device, given by the series of amendments to R148 under which it is approved (see Table 2).
The change index for rear position, stop and reversing lamps is 0 for the 00 series of amendments and 1 for the 01 series.
Every device of an approved type must have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings required by paragraphs 3.3.3.2 to 3.3.3.6.
All markings must be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking dimension 'a' must be at least 5 mm.
The lamp's approval marking must include a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
The approval marking must include the four to six-digit sequential number that is part of the approval number. It must be placed close to the approval mark.

The approval marking must include the symbols identifying the light-signalling lamp functions approved under paragraph 3.2.4. For this product these would be the rear position, stop and reversing functions.
The approval marking must include the number of R148 followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits of the amendment series in force when the approval was issued.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp that is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking, and the category or categories of any prescribed LED substitute light source(s), shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.
Affix the approval marking, and the markings in 3.3.3.2, 3.3.3.3, 3.3.3.4, 3.3.3.5(b) and 3.3.3.6, on the lamp.

The markings in 3.3.3.2, 3.3.3.3(a), 3.3.3.4, 3.3.3.5 and 3.3.3.6 need not meet the 3.3.4.2 visibility-when-fitted requirement. Only the approval marking and any LED substitute light source category marking must be visible.

If a single approval mark is used for the combined lamps, it may be located anywhere on the group only if it meets the visibility and non-removability conditions that follow in 3.3.5.1.1 and 3.3.5.1.2.
The single approval mark on the combined lamps must be visible after installation.
No light-transmitting part of the combined lamps may be removable without also removing the approval mark.
The components of a single approval mark must be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks under the relevant UN Regulations.
Notify the Type Approval Authority that approved the type of every modification of the lamp type.
Conformity of production procedures must comply with the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), with the requirements set out in paragraph 6.
The lamp must continue to meet the Regulation's requirements, otherwise the approval granted may be withdrawn.
If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture a lamp approved under this Regulation, it must inform the authority that granted the approval.
Each lamp submitted for approval must conform to the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5.

Apply the pertinent requirements of sections 5 and 6 of UN R48 (and the other listed Regulations) for each lamp function and vehicle category (M1). Apply them where verification at lamp type approval is feasible.
Design and construct the lamp so that, in normal use and despite vibration, satisfactory operation is assured and the characteristics prescribed by the Regulation are retained.
In a single lamp with more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that failure of any one makes all stop emitting light is treated as one light source.

On failure of any one light source in a single lamp with more than one light source, either the intensity still meets the minimum in the standard light distribution table (Annex 3) and the maximum is not exceeded with all sources lit, or a failure tell-tale signal is produced, with a communication-form note that the lamp is only for vehicles fitted with such a tell-tale.

The lamp may only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved under UN R37, R99 and/or R128 (with no use restriction declared at application), light source modules, and/or non-replaceable light sources.

The light signalling device must not generate radiated or power line disturbances that cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle. EMC compliance is assessed at vehicle-type level.
All photometric and colorimetric measurements must be made under the conditions of paragraph 4.8, using the methods of Annex 3.
For a lamp with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), all measurements must be made with the light source(s) present in the lamp.
Stray reflections must be avoided by appropriate masking during photometric measurements.
Unless otherwise specified, measure intensities with the light source continuously lit.
If results are challenged, measure at a distance where the inverse square law of distance applies.
If results are challenged, use measuring equipment whose receiver angular aperture, seen from the reference centre, is between 10' and 1 degree.
An intensity requirement for a direction is deemed met if it is met within 1/4 degree of that direction.
Determine the limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the light-signalling lamp.
Unless otherwise specified, supply the lamp at 6.75 V (6 V systems), 13.5 V (12 V systems) or 28 V (24 V systems) for testing.
For lamps without electronic control gear or variable intensity control that use light source modules or non-replaceable light sources, operate the lamp as specified by the applicant.
Record the voltage applied, with tolerances, in the Annex 1 communication form. Also record any electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control, if applicable.
On the reference axis (HV), the intensity of each of the two samples must be not less than the minimum in the table for the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
In no direction where the lamp is visible may the intensity exceed the maximum in the table for the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

Outside the reference axis, the intensity must be not less than the table minimum multiplied by the percentage in the Annex 3 light distribution figure, or not less than the value given in that figure, for each direction in question. Within the Annex 2 geometric visibility angles it must be not less than the table minimum.
Tests for compliance of the luminous intensities must be carried out according to Annex 8.

Measure the colour of the emitted light inside the field of the Annex 3 light distribution grid for the specific function, using the paragraph 4.8 test procedure. No sharp colour variation may be observed outside this field.

The light from each of the two rear position lamp samples must meet the Table 4 luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements. A maximum of 60 cd is permitted only for a position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, below a plane 5° downward from horizontal.

The rear position lamp must meet the Table 4 values for its category (R1 or R2). R1 is 4 cd minimum and 17 cd maximum as a single lamp. R2 is 4 cd minimum and 42 cd maximum as a single lamp. Both use the Figure A3-I distribution and a 0.05 cd minimum within the geometric visibility angles.
Minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility must meet Table 4 (5·10^-2 cd).
The rear position lamp must emit red light.
Stop lamp samples must meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.

The stop lamp must meet the minimum and maximum luminous intensity, standard light distribution and geometric visibility values in Table 7 for its category. The category is not stated in the spec, but S1 or S2 is expected for a rear lamp.
The stop lamp must meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility given in Table 7.
The stop lamp must meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The stop lamp must emit red light.

Light emitted by each of the two samples supplied of the reversing lamp must meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 10. A reduced check (up to 30° inwards, at least 2.5·10^1 cd) is allowed only if the lamp is intended for installation exclusively as a pair. This must be declared in the application and shown in the communication form.

The reversing lamp (AR) must meet the Table 10 photometric values. Minimum intensity is 8.0·10^1 cd. Maximum intensity is 3.00·10^2 cd in or above the h-plane. Maximum intensity is 6.00·10^2 cd below the h-plane down to 5°D. Maximum intensity is 8.00·10^3 cd below 5°D. The standard light distribution is Figure A3-V.
The reversing lamp shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The reversing lamp shall emit white light.
Lamps must be manufactured to conform to the type approved under this Regulation. Compliance with the paragraph 5 requirements is verified as set out in 6.1.1 to 6.1.3.
Production must comply with the minimum requirements for conformity of production control procedures in Annex 4.
Production must comply with the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 5.

For conformity of production, no measured photometric value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in R148. Table 12 gives the equivalent values for the minimum values required in the fields of Annexes 2 and 3.

For conformity of production, minimum required intensities (e.g. 7·10^-1, 6·10^-1, 3·10^-1, 7·10^-2, 5·10^-2 cd) must be met within the equivalent 20 per cent values (5·10^-1, 4·10^-1, 2·10^-1, 5·10^-2, 3·10^-2 cd). The table also lists 30 per cent values.
The production facility's conformity control methods may be verified by the approving authority at any time. The normal frequency is once every two years.

The type approval of each R148 lamp function (stop, position, reversing) must be documented in the Annex 1 communication, which states the lamp function, its category, the change index and the approval number.
The approval communication must state the trade name or mark of the lamp.
The approval communication must state the manufacturer's name for the type of lamp.
The approval communication must state the manufacturer's name and address.
If applicable, state the name and address of the manufacturer's representative in the approval communication.
Record the date the lamp type was submitted for approval in the communication.
Identify the Technical Service responsible for conducting approval tests in the communication.
State the date of the test report issued by the Technical Service in the communication.
State the number of the test report issued by the Technical Service in the communication.
For a reversing lamp, declare in the communication whether the lamp shall be installed on a vehicle only as part of a pair of lamps (yes/no).

For each light signalling function and category of the lamp (position, stop, reversing), the communication must state mounting, colour of light emitted, and the number, category and kind of light source(s). It must also give the LED substitute and light source module status, voltage, control gear and related details.
The communication must declare whether the rear position, stop and reversing lamps are only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure (yes/no).
The communication must state the position of the approval mark on the lamp.

The rear position lamp (category R1/R2) must provide the minimum angles of geometric visibility in Table A2-1: 45°/80° horizontal (20°/80° below the H-plane for lamps mounted below 750 mm) and 15°/15° vertical (15°/5° if the H-plane is below 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps above 2,100 mm).

The stop lamp (category S1/S2) must provide the minimum angles of geometric visibility in Table A2-1: 45°/45° horizontal (20°/45° below the H-plane for lamps mounted below 750 mm) and 15°/15° vertical (15°/5° if the H-plane is below 750 mm; 5°/15° for optional lamps above 2,100 mm).

Photometric intensities must meet the minimum percentages shown in Figures A3-I to A3-XV, measured relative to the reference axis (H=0°, V=0°). For rear position lamps and S1/S2/MS stop lamps mounted at a height of 750 mm or less, verification extends only to 5° downwards.

Within the grid field of light distribution, the pattern must be substantially uniform. The intensity in each direction must meet at least the lowest minimum value shown on the surrounding grid lines.

For reversing lamps showing substantial local intensity variations on visual examination, check that no intensity between two measurement directions is below 50% of the lower of the two prescribed minimums.

The rear position lamp and the stop lamp (S1, S2 or MS) must meet the standard light distribution. The minimum intensities in each direction are the percentages shown, applied to the minimum intensities required by the relevant Tables.
The rear position and stop lamp light distribution must conform to the standard distribution in Figure A3-I.
The reversing lamp must meet the standard light distribution: the minimum intensities at the specified measuring points, in degrees from the axis of reference.

The reversing lamp must give at least the minimum intensities in cd shown in figure A3-V at the measurement directions. H=0°/V=0° is the axis of reference, horizontal and parallel to the vehicle median longitudinal plane.
Conformity of production is satisfied mechanically and geometrically if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of the Regulation.
The photometric conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested when a randomly chosen lamp is tested for photometric performance according to paragraph 4.8.
Chromaticity coordinates must be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of the Regulation.

For each lamp type, the type-approval holder must carry out at least the specified tests at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the Regulation. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and tested, and the manufacturer must take steps to ensure production conformity.
Manufacturer conformity tests must cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the test methods set out in UN R148.

Equivalent methods may be used in the manufacturer's conformity tests only with the consent of the competent authority. The manufacturer must prove the applied methods are equivalent to those in the Regulation.
Test apparatus must be calibrated regularly, and its measurements must be correlated with those of the competent authority.
The reference test methods are always those of UN R148, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.

Lamp samples must be selected at random from a uniform batch of the same type. Assessment generally covers series production of individual factories. Records from several factories may be grouped only if they operate under the same quality system and management.
Sampled lamps must be measured for photometric minimum values at the Annex 3 points and for the required chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of the test results and define acceptability criteria with the competent authority. The criteria must give a minimum 0.95 probability of passing an Annex 5 spot check at a 95% confidence level.
Mechanical and geometric conformity requirements are satisfied if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

On a randomly chosen lamp, no measured photometric value may deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3. For lamps with a replaceable light source, a failed test is repeated with another standard light source.
Chromaticity coordinates of mass-produced lamps shall comply when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of the Regulation.

Conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if the deviation of every specimen in samples A and B (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be terminated if both lamps of sample A deviate by not more than 0 per cent.

If any specimen of sample A or B deviates by more than 20 per cent, conformity is contested. The manufacturer must bring production into line, and repeated sampling is carried out within two months of notification. Samples A and B are retained by the Technical Service until the CoP process ends.

Conformity is not contested if the deviation of every specimen in samples C and D (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be terminated if both lamps of sample C deviate by not more than 0 per cent.

If deviation is more than 20 per cent but no specimen exceeds 30 per cent, the manufacturer must align production again. A second repeated sampling follows within two months of notification, and samples C and D are retained by the Technical Service until the CoP process is finished.
If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 applied.

Conformity is not contested if the deviation of every specimen in samples E and F (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be terminated if both lamps of sample E deviate by not more than 0 per cent.
Conformity of mass-produced lamps is contested if at least one specimen of samples E or F deviates by more than 20 per cent. In that case the approval is withdrawn.
Where the Annex 5 paragraph 4.1 and 4.2 criteria require it, approval of the lamp is withdrawn according to paragraph 3.6 of the Regulation.
For the reversing lamp with non-incandescent (LED) light source, luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation must comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For the position and stop lamps (non-incandescent, LED), luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability must comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
In addition to paragraph 1, luminous intensity distribution must be checked for compliance at the point in time listed in Table A8-1, depending on the light source technology.

Additional photometric checks are done at the listed time after switch-on at the reference coordinate. For the product's functions the table gives front and rear position 4 s at HV, stop 0.2 s at HV, and reversing 0.2 s at HV.
For a lamp function that uses LED technology only, the intensity requirements are deemed met at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 comply.
The retro-reflector integrated in the rear lamp is a retro-reflective device within the scope and must meet the Regulation as a Class IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB or IVA retro-reflector.
The type approval application must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark, or by his duly accredited representative, with the required documents.

Submit drawings in triplicate, detailed enough to identify the type. They must show the positions in which the retro-reflector may be fitted. For Class IB, they must also give installation details and the position of the approval number and class indicator relative to the approval mark circle.
Submit a brief description of the technical specifications of the materials of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
Submit samples of the retro-reflector in the colour specified by the manufacturer, with fixation means if necessary. The number of samples is set in paragraphs 5.1 and 5.2.
A separate approval is required for each retro-reflective device listed in paragraph 1.
Notice of approval, extension, refusal or withdrawal of the device type must be communicated using the form conforming to the Annex 1 model.
The approval number assigned to the approved type must be marked on the device per paragraph 3.3.
The retro-reflector must be identified in Annex 1 by the symbol assigned to its device class in the listed symbols.

The retro-reflector combined with other signal lamps in the housing must carry the symbol for its class (IB for a motor-vehicle retro-reflector combined with signal lamps that are not watertight, or IA if independent). The marking size 'a' is at least 5 mm.
The change index for the device must correspond to the series of amendments applied, as listed in the change index table.
The change index for the combined motor-vehicle retro-reflector is 0 under the 00 series and 1 under the 01 series of amendments.
The device must have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking (Unique Identifier) and the other required markings.
All markings must be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking size must use the value 'a' from Table 1 (at least 5 mm for classes IA and IB retro-reflectors).
The approval marking must include a circle surrounding the letter E followed by the distinguishing number of the approving country.
The four to six-digit sequential number of the approval number must be placed close to the approval mark.
The approval marking must include the symbol(s) identifying the retro-reflective device, as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.
The approval marking must include the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter R and the two digits of the amendment series in force at the time of approval.
If the approval marking is replaced by a Unique Identifier, the UI mark must follow the prescribed format (Figure I).
Retro-reflective devices must bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

For a Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA retro-reflector, the word TOP must be inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if this is necessary to determine without ambiguity the rotation angle(s) the manufacturer prescribes.
The approval marking or Unique Identifier, and the markings in 3.3.4, must be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.

If the grouped or combined lamps comply with several UN Regulations, a single approval mark (four to six-digit sequential number or Unique Identifier) may be affixed. It may be placed anywhere on the lamps, subject to the conditions in 3.3.6.1.1 and 3.3.6.1.2.
The single approval mark on the grouped or combined lamp must be visible after installation.
No light-transmitting part of the grouped or combined lamp may be removable without also removing the single approval mark.
The components of a single approval mark must be no smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest individual mark under the relevant UN Regulations.
Every modification of the type of retro-reflective device must be notified to the Type Approval Authority that approved the type.
Conformity of production procedures must comply with those in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), together with the additional requirements that follow in the Regulation.
Retro-reflectors approved under R150 must be manufactured to conform to the approved type, meeting the requirements of paragraphs 4 and 5.
Retro-reflector production must meet the minimum conformity-of-production control procedure requirements in Annex 2.
Retro-reflector production must meet the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 3.
The production facility must accept verification of its conformity control methods by the approval authority at any time, normally once every two years.

Apply the requirements of sections 5 and 6 and the referenced Annexes of UN Regulations 48, 53, 74 or 86 (as in force at application) that are pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and the vehicle category, where verification at type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflective devices must function satisfactorily and continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices must not have any design or manufacturing defect detrimental to their efficient operation or maintenance in good condition.
Components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof must not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of the retro-reflector must be easy to clean. It must not be rough, and any protuberances must not prevent easy cleaning.
There must be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector in normal use.
The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter must not be coloured by paint or varnish.

The retro-reflector is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A (1/3° divergence, β1=β2=0°, or the Annex 4 Part 1 angle if surface reflection is colourless). The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected light must be within the UN R48 night-time colour limits.

Each Class IA/IB retro-reflector, tested per 5.1.7, must meet the Annex 5 dimension and shape requirements, the photometric and colorimetric requirements of 5.1.4 to 5.1.5, and the physical and mechanical requirements, depending on materials and construction.
The applicant must submit ten retro-reflector samples for approval, to be tested in the chronological order given in 5.1.7.

The ten retro-reflector samples must undergo the heat resistance test (Annex 6 Part 1), then colorimetric and RI examination at least one hour later. The remaining samples are then split into groups for the water penetration, fuel and lubricant, corrosion (if necessary), abrasion, optical stability and weathering tests.
After the tests in 5.1.3.1, each retro-reflector group must still have a colour that satisfies paragraph 5.1.5.

After the tests, each retro-reflector group must have an RI meeting 5.1.4. Verification is only at 20' divergence and β1 = β2 = 0°, or if necessary in all positions in Annex 4 Part 1, paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2.
When applying for approval, the applicant must specify one or more axes of reference, or a range, corresponding to illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° in the RI table.
If the manufacturer specifies more than one axis of reference or a range, the photometric measurements must be repeated for each different axis, or for the extreme axes of the range.

For photometric measurement of a Class IA/IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface within a 200 mm diameter circle is considered, limited to 100 cm2. The manufacturer must specify the perimeter of the area used.
Red Class IA/IB retro-reflectors must have RI values at or above Table 3 (mcd/lx) at the stated divergence and illumination angles, measured per paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4.

Red Class IA/IB retro-reflector minimum RI: at 20' divergence, 300 (0°/0°), 200 (±10°/0°), 100 (±5°/±20°) mcd/lx. At 1°30', 5, 2.8, 2.5 mcd/lx. RI values lower than those in the last two columns are not permitted within the solid angle bounded by the planes along (β1=±10°, β2=0°) and (β1=±5°, β2=±20°).
Test the night-time colour of the retro-reflector according to the method in paragraph 4.2.1.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected light must be within the UN R48 limits for the night-time colour (red for a rear retro-reflector).
Type-approval testing of Class IA/IB retro-reflector samples follows the Table 4 order, starting with a general specifications visual inspection on all samples.

Class IA/IB retro-reflector samples undergo the Table 4 tests in the stated order: shapes and dimensions inspection, heat, colorimetry, photometry, water, motor fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time and weathering, with the stated intermediate colorimetry and photometry checks.

In the approval communication, describe the retro-reflector device, including whether it is installed as an integral part of a lamp integrated into the vehicle body, the colour of light emitted, whether it is in isolation or part of an assembly, the geometric installation conditions, and whether the mounting height is 750 mm or less.
State the position of the approval mark or Unique Identifier (UI) in the approval communication.
Mass-produced retro-reflectors must conform mechanically and geometrically to the approved type. Differences may not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the Regulation's requirements.
For a retro-reflector chosen at random, no measured photometric value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the prescribed minimum values.
The chromaticity coordinates of the retro-reflector must be complied with.

For each retro-reflector type, the approval mark holder must carry out at least the specified tests at appropriate intervals, following the Regulation. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and the manufacturer must act to restore conformity.
Manufacturer conformity tests must cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.
Conformity tests must generally follow the methods set out in the Regulation.
Equivalent test methods may be used only with the consent of the Type Approval Authority. The manufacturer must prove that the methods are equivalent to those in the Regulation.
Test apparatus must be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a Type Approval Authority.
The reference test methods are always those of the Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
Retro-reflector samples must be selected at random from a uniform batch of the same type, defined by the manufacturer's production methods.
Sampled retro-reflective devices must be photometrically measured at the points and chromaticity coordinates provided for in the Regulation.
The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of the test results and define acceptability criteria in agreement with the Type Approval Authority.
For conformity, no measured photometric value of a randomly chosen retro-reflective device may deviate unfavourably by more than 20% from the prescribed minimum values.
The chromaticity coordinates must be complied with in conformity checks.

In the first sampling, four retro-reflective devices are selected at random (samples A and B). If the deviation exceeds 20%, the manufacturer must align production and a repeated sampling is carried out within two months.
After the first repeated sampling (samples C and D), conformity is not contested if no specimen deviates by more than 20%.
Conformity of mass-produced retro-reflective devices is contested if the deviation criteria listed in 3.2.1 and 3.2.2 are met.

If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20% but all deviate by no more than 30%, the manufacturer must realign production and a second repeated sampling is carried out within two months.
If one specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 30%, approval is withdrawn.
After the second repeated sampling (samples E and F), conformity is not contested if no specimen deviates by more than 20%.
If one specimen of samples E or F deviates by more than 20%, approval is withdrawn.
One retro-reflector of sample A must pass the resistance-to-water-penetration test of Annex 6 Part 2 para 1. If it fails, both retro-reflective devices of sample B must be tested and both must pass.
When measuring RI at β1 = β2 = 0°, check for a mirror effect by slightly turning the device. If there is one, take the reading at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.

For retro-reflective devices not marked "TOP", rotate the device about its reference axis to the position of minimum RI. That RI must meet the specified value. If the value is not reached, the device may be rotated ±5° from that position.
For retro-reflective devices marked "TOP", rotate the device ±5° about its axes. RI must not fall below the prescribed value in any position during this rotation.
If RI at β1=β2=0° and ε=0° exceeds the specified value by 50% or more, make all measurements for all angles of illumination and divergence at ε=0°.
Use the CIE-angular system (Figure A4-I) to specify and measure the retro-reflective device.
Illuminate the retro-reflective device with CIE Standard Illuminant A when testing retro-reflection. Measure as described in Part 1 of Annex 4.
Measure within these limits: source angular diameter δ≤10', measuring device angular diameter γ≤10', and illuminated area angular diameter η≤80'.
Avoid stray reflections during photometric measurements by appropriate masking.
Choose the photometric measuring distance so that at least the angle limits for δ, γ and η (Figure A4-III) are respected, and use a distance of at least 10 m.

Illuminance over the useful area of the retro-reflective device must be sufficiently uniform. It is checked with a measuring element no larger than one-tenth of the area examined, and max/min must be ≤ 1.05.
The photometer head must be corrected to the spectral luminous efficiency of the CIE standard photometric observer in photopic vision.
The photometer device must show no perceptible change in local sensitivity within its aperture. Otherwise suitable provisions, such as a diffusing window, must be added.
Restrict the photometer head's field of view and the spread of light from the sample and the source as much as possible to minimise stray light.
Screen reflections from the floor and walls from both the sample and the photometer head with baffles.

Measure residual stray light with the sample covered by an opaque matt black surface, zigzag folded black paper of the same size and shape, or a suitably oriented specular black surface with a light trap. Subtract this value from the value measured on the retro-reflective device.
The illuminating surface of the retro-reflector must not be easily confused with the triangular shape prescribed for Class IIIA/IIIB retro-reflectors, when viewed from 10 metres.
Moulded plastics retro-reflector (Classes IA, IB etc.) must be kept 48 consecutive hours dry at 65 °C ± 2 °C, then cooled 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device, in particular its optical component, may be visible.

Retro-reflective device, whether part of a lamp or not, stripped of removable parts, is immersed 10 min in 50 ± 5 °C water (top of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface), repeated turned 180°, then immediately immersed in 25 ± 5 °C water.
No water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. Visible water means the test is failed.

The retro-reflective device must keep its prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences it is normally exposed to. Check the front surface's resistance to tarnishing and the rear face protection against deterioration. Corrosion testing follows ISO 9227:2017.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if combined with a light, must be stripped of removable parts. It is then exposed to saline mist for 50 hours: two 24-hour exposures separated by a 2-hour drying interval.
Immediately after the saline-mist corrosion test, the sample must not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
Weathering apparatus must comply with EN ISO 4892-1:2016 and EN ISO 4892-2:2013. It must control temperature and relative humidity and have a water spray system.
The water spray system must be able to spray at least 0.3 ml/cm² within 5 minutes.
The spray water must meet the requirements of EN ISO 4892-2:2013.
Temperature is measured with either a Black-Standard thermometer (TM1) or a Black-Panel thermometer (TM2).
The weathering test method used (TM1 or TM2) must be specified in the report.
Retro-reflective device samples must be exposed per EN ISO 4892-2:2013 using the Table A6-1 parameters for 500 hours.

The weathering exposure must use the Table A6-1 parameters: 102 min dry and 18 min water spray cycles, irradiance 60±2 W/m² broadband and 0.51±0.02 W/m² at 340 nm, and 50±10 % RH. Black-standard temperature is 65±3 °C (TM1) and black-panel temperature is 63±3 °C (TM2).
The fuel resistance test uses a mixture of 70 vol.% n-heptane and 30 vol.% toluol.
Lightly wipe the retro-reflector's outer surface, especially the illuminating surface, with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture.
After about five minutes, visually inspect the surface. There must be no apparent surface changes, though slight surface cracks are not objected to.

Wipe the outer surface of the retro-reflector, especially the illuminating surface, with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil. After about 5 minutes, clean the surface. Then measure RI according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2.
The application for approval must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark, or by their duly accredited representative.

Submit drawings in triplicate, in enough detail to identify the reversing lamp type. They must show the mounting geometry, the axis of reference, the centre of reference, and the position of the approval mark.

Submit a brief technical description stating the prescribed filament lamp category, LED light source category, or light source module identification code. Lamps with non-replaceable light sources are excepted.
Submit two samples of the reversing lamp. Symmetrical left and right devices may be submitted as two identical samples for one side.
Lamps submitted for approval must bear the applicant's trade name or mark, clearly legible and indelible.
Provide adequate space for the approval mark and the additional symbols, shown in the drawing under 2.2.1.
The approved reversing lamp must bear, in the reserved space, the international approval mark (circle with E and country number, plus approval number) in addition to the marks in 3.1–3.3 or 3.5.
Reversing lamps must bear the additional symbol of letters A and R, arranged as shown in Annex 2.

Each lamp in a grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated assembly must satisfy this Regulation or another applicable Regulation. A lamp that satisfies none of them must not be part of the assembly.

Where the combined lamps comply with several Regulations, a single international approval mark (E circle, country number, approval number and, if necessary, the arrow) may be applied anywhere on the assembly, subject to the visibility and non-removability conditions.
The single approval mark on the combined lamp assembly must be visible after installation.
The approval mark must be positioned so that no light-transmitting part of the combined assembly can be removed without also removing the mark.
Mark the identification symbol for each lamp, appropriate to each Regulation under which approval has been granted, together with the corresponding series of amendments.
For the combined lamp assembly, the identification symbol of each lamp is marked either on the appropriate light-emitting surface, or (per 4.5.2.2) in a group.
If marked as a group, the marking must let each lamp of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps be clearly identified (examples in annex 2).
The components of a single approval mark must not be smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks under the Regulations under which approval was granted.
An approval number is assigned to each approved type of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps. The same Contracting Party may not give the same number to another type.
The approval mark and symbol must be indelible and clearly legible, even when the reversing lamp is mounted on the vehicle.

The pertinent requirements of R48 or R86 (sections 5 and 6 and the referenced annexes, in the series in force at application) apply to each lamp and to the vehicle category, where verification at type approval is feasible.
Each sample must conform to the specifications in the paragraphs below.
The reversing lamp must be designed and built to keep working satisfactorily and keep its prescribed characteristics in normal use despite vibration.
The intensity of the light emitted by each of the two samples must be within the specified minima and maxima, measured relative to the axis of reference in the specified directions.
Intensity along the axis of reference must be at least 80 candelas.
Intensity in all observable directions must not exceed 300 cd at or above the horizontal plane, 600 cd between h-h and 5° D, and 8,000 cd below 5° D.

In the other measurement directions of annex 3, luminous intensity must meet the annex minima. Verification only up to 30° inwards with at least 25 cd is allowed only if the lamp is installed exclusively in a pair, and this must be declared in the application and the communication form.
For a reversing lamp containing more than one light source, the maximum intensities must not be exceeded when all light sources are illuminated.

On failure of any one light source in a lamp with more than one light source, either the Annex 3 minimum intensity is still met, or a failure tell-tale signal (R48 6.4.8) is produced. The tell-tale option requires at least 50% of the minimum intensity on the axis of reference and a communication-form note limiting use to vehicles fitted with a tell-tale.
All photometric and colorimetric measurements of the reversing lamp must be made under the conditions of paragraphs 7.1.1 to 7.1.4.
Provide the Technical Service with the light source control gear needed to supply the light source and the applicable functions.
The voltage to be applied to the lamp must be indicated in the communication form specified in Annex 1.

For lamps not equipped with filament lamps, luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes must meet the minimum and maximum requirements. The distribution is calculated from the distribution measured after photometric stability, using the HV intensity ratios. Photometric stability means variation below 3% within any 15 minute period.
Determine the limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the light-signalling device.

Light from the reversing lamp inside the Annex 3 light distribution grid must be white, with no sharp colour variation outside the field. Colorimetric characteristics are verified using the paragraph 7 test procedure. For lamps with non-replaceable light sources, they are verified with the light sources present in the lamp.
Conformity of production procedures must comply with Appendix 2 of the 1958 Agreement and the further requirements that follow in this clause.
Lamps must be manufactured to conform to the approved type. Compliance with paragraphs 6 and 8 must be verified.
Comply with the minimum conformity of production control requirements in Annex 4.
Comply with the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 5.
Production facilities must allow the approval authority to verify conformity control methods at any time. The normal frequency is once every two years.
Production reversing lamps must conform to the approved type and carry the approval marks. Otherwise the approval may be withdrawn.
If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture an approved type of reversing lamp, it shall inform the authority that granted the approval.

The approval communication for the reversing lamp must include a concise description: number, category and kind of light source(s), voltage and wattage, electronic control gear and light source module details, and installation conditions.
The communication must state the position of the approval mark on the lamp.
For a reversing lamp, the communication must state (yes/no) whether the device shall be installed on a vehicle only as part of a pair of devices.

For a lighting device in which two or more lamps are grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated, the approval mark may follow the simplified marking models B, C or D. The mark identifies each function, including the reversing lamp (AR) approved under R23.
Avoid stray reflections during photometric measurements by appropriate masking.

If results are challenged, measure at a distance where the inverse-square law applies. The receiver must subtend 10' to 1° from the reference centre. The intensity requirement is met if the required intensity is obtained within 1/4° of the direction of observation.

Take photometric measurements relative to the reference axis (H=0°, V=0°). On the vehicle this axis is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane and oriented in the required direction of visibility. It passes through the centre of reference. The reversing lamp must meet the minimum intensities in cd given in the table for each direction of measurement.

If visual examination reveals substantial local variations of intensity, check that no intensity measured between two prescribed measurement directions is below 50 per cent of the lower of the two prescribed minimum intensities.
Mechanical and geometric conformity is satisfied if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of the Regulation.

Conformity of production is not contested if, for a randomly chosen lamp tested photometrically per paragraph 7, no measured value deviates unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the prescribed values.
Chromaticity coordinates must be complied with when tested under the conditions of paragraph 7.

For each lamp type, the approval mark holder must carry out at least the specified tests at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the Regulation. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and the manufacturer must take steps to ensure production conformity.
Conformity tests must cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Tests must generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
Equivalent test methods may be used only with the consent of the competent authority. The manufacturer must prove that the methods are equivalent to those in the Regulation.
Test apparatus must be calibrated regularly, and its results correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
The reference methods in all cases must be those of this Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
Lamp samples must be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch, meaning lamps of the same type as defined by the manufacturer's production methods.
The sampled lamp must undergo photometric measurements for the minimum values at the points listed in Annex 3 and for the required chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of test results and define acceptability criteria, in agreement with the competent authority. The criteria must give, with 95% confidence, a minimum probability of 0.95 of passing an Annex 5 spot check on first sampling.
Mass-produced reversing lamps must conform mechanically and geometrically to the Regulation, with differences no greater than inevitable manufacturing deviations.
Photometric conformity of mass-produced reversing lamps is judged on a randomly chosen lamp, tested per paragraph 7 against the photometric performance in paragraph 6.
The requirements in paragraph 1.2.1 of Annex 4 must be met for conformity of production.
Lamps with apparent defects are disregarded in the photometric conformity sampling.
Chromaticity coordinates must comply when tested under the conditions of paragraph 7.
In the first sampling, four lamps are selected at random, as two samples of two marked A and B.

Conformity is not contested if the deviation of every specimen in samples A and B (all four lamps) is no more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample A deviate by no more than 0 per cent.

If at least one specimen of sample A or B deviates by more than 20 per cent, conformity is contested. The manufacturer must align production, and repeated sampling is carried out within two months of notification. Samples A and B are retained until the process ends.
For the first repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment, as samples C and D of two each.

Conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample C deviate by no more than 0 per cent.
Conformity of mass-produced lamps shall be contested if the deviations set out in the sub-paragraphs occur.

If one specimen of sample C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent but none by more than 30 per cent, the manufacturer must align production. A second repeated sampling must then be carried out within two months of notification. Samples C and D are retained by the Technical Service until conformity of production is finished.
If one specimen of samples C and D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval is withdrawn and paragraph 5 applies.
For the second repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment. The first two are marked E and the second two are marked F.

Conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples E and F (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20 per cent. Measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample E deviate by no more than 0 per cent.
Conformity is contested if at least one specimen of samples E or F deviates by more than 20 per cent. The approval is then withdrawn and paragraph 5 applies.
Approval is withdrawn in accordance with paragraph 10 of the Regulation.

The external surface, including the rear lamp, must not have outward-directed pointed or sharp parts or projections whose shape, dimensions, direction or hardness would increase the risk or seriousness of injury in a collision.
The external surface, including the rear lamp, must not have outward-directed parts likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

Protruding parts of the external surface, including the rear lamp, must have a radius of curvature of at least 2.5 mm. Parts protruding less than 5 mm are exempt from this, but their outward-facing angles must be blunted unless they protrude less than 1.5 mm.

If the projection of a component on a non-convex surface cannot be determined by simple measurement, determine it as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal panel line. The sphere is moved over the component in constant contact with it.

The application for approval must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark, or by an accredited representative. It must be accompanied by drawings in triplicate sufficient to identify the type, a description of the optical unit materials, and samples of the device.
Every retro-reflecting device submitted for approval must bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
The word "TOP" must be inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface if it is needed to determine the prescribed rotation angle(s) without ambiguity.
A space of sufficient size for the approval mark must be provided on every device and shown on the drawings.
The markings must be visible from the outside when the retro-reflecting device is fitted on the vehicle.
Markings on the retro-reflecting device must be clearly legible and indelible.

The retro-reflector type must carry an approval number assigned by the approving Contracting Party. Its first two digits indicate the series of amendments, and the same number is not assigned to another type except for a colour-only extension.

The retro-reflecting device must carry an international approval mark, which is a circle around the letter E followed by the distinguishing number of the approving country. It is placed in the space provided and added to the other prescribed markings.
The mark must include the approval number and the class symbol (IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB or IVA) of the approved retro-reflecting device.

For a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps including a retro-reflector, approval is granted only if each lamp satisfies UN R3 or another Regulation. A lamp that satisfies none of them cannot be part of the unit.

If a single international approval mark is used for the combined lamps, it consists of the E-circle with the country number, the approval number and, if necessary, the required arrow. It must satisfy the placement conditions in 5.6.1.1 and 5.6.1.2.
The single approval mark on the combined lamp must be visible after installation.
No light-transmitting part of the combined lamp can be removed without also removing the approval mark.

Mark the identification symbol of each lamp for each Regulation under which approval is granted, together with the corresponding series of amendments. Placement is on the light-emitting surface or in a group, per 5.6.2.1 and 5.6.2.2.
For grouped/combined lamps, the identification symbol of each lamp may be marked on the appropriate light-emitting surface (one of two alternatives).
If marked as a group, the marking must allow each lamp of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps to be clearly identified (examples in Annex 3).
The components of a single approval mark must not be smaller than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks under the Regulations by which approval was granted.
An approval number is assigned to each approved type. The same Contracting Party may not assign the same number to another type of grouped/combined lamps.
The approval mark must be clearly legible and indelible.

The retro-reflecting device must meet the pertinent requirements of sections 5 and 6 and the referenced Annexes of Regulations 48, 53, 74 or 86 (series of amendments in force at the time of application). These apply for the vehicle category concerned, where verification at type approval is feasible.

The retro-reflecting device must be constructed to function satisfactorily and continue to do so in normal use, with no design or manufacturing defect detrimental to efficient operation or maintenance in good condition.
The components of the retro-reflecting device must not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The retro-reflecting optical units may not be replaceable.
The outer surface of the retro-reflecting device must be easy to clean: not rough, and any protuberances must not prevent easy cleaning.
There must be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.

The retro-reflecting device must satisfy the dimensional and shape, colorimetric, photometric, physical and mechanical requirements in Annexes 5 to 11 and 13. The test procedures are in Annex 4 (Class IA, IIIA), Annex 14 (Class IVA) or Annex 16 (Class IB, IIIB), depending on its class.
Retro-reflectors must be manufactured to conform to the type approved under this Regulation. Compliance with the requirements of paragraphs 6 and 7 is verified as set out in the sub-clauses.
Conformity of production control procedures must meet the minimum requirements in Annex 17.
Sampling by an inspector must meet the minimum requirements in Annex 18.
A retro-reflecting device bearing the approval mark must conform to the approved type and the Regulation's requirements, or its approval may be withdrawn.

Provide a concise description of the retro-reflecting device in the communication. State whether it is in isolation or part of an assembly, the colour of light emitted, whether it is installed as an integral part of a lamp integrated into the vehicle body, the geometric installation conditions, and whether the mounting height is limited to 750 mm or less.
State the position of the approval mark on the retro-reflecting device in the communication.
Compliance of the retro-reflector with the Annex 5 shape and dimension specifications must be verified by visual inspection.
Where the retro-reflecting device combines an optical unit and a filter, it must be designed so the two cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The colouring of retro-reflecting optical units and filters by paint or varnish is not permitted.

When illuminated by CIE illuminant A with 1/3 degree divergence at V=H=0 degrees (or V=±5 degrees, H=0 if there is colourless surface reflection), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected light must lie within the limits of paragraph 2.30 of UN R48.

The applicant must specify one or more axes of reference (or a range) corresponding to V=H=0 degrees. If more than one is specified, the photometric measurements must be repeated for each, or for the extreme axes of a range.

For photometric measurement, only the illuminating surface specified by the manufacturer is considered. For Class IA/IB it must lie within a 200 mm diameter circle and is limited to 100 cm2. The manufacturer must specify the perimeter of the area used.

CIL values for red retro-reflecting devices must be at least those in the table (for Class IA/IB: 300/200/100 mcd/lx at 20' and 5/2.8/2.5 mcd/lx at 1°30', for the stated illumination angles). Lower values are not permitted within the specified solid angle.
When measuring CIL at V = H = 0°, check whether slightly turning the device produces a mirror effect. If it does, take a reading at V = ±5°, H = 0°, and adopt the position giving the minimum CIL.
If CIL at V = H = 0° and ε = 0° exceeds the specified value by 50% or more, make all measurements for all illumination and divergence angles at ε = 0°.

Retro-reflecting device, stripped of removable parts, is immersed for 10 min in water at 50±5 °C with the highest point of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface. Repeat after turning it 180°, then immediately immerse it in water at 25±5 °C under the same conditions.
After the water submersion test, no water may penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit. If visual inspection clearly shows water, the device fails.

If visual inspection shows no water, or in case of doubt, measure the CIL by the Annex 4 para 3.2 or Annex 14 para 4.2 method. First lightly shake the retro-reflecting device to remove excess water from the outside.

Retro-reflecting devices must be designed to keep the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite humidity and corrosive influences. Front-surface resistance to tarnishing and rear-face protection against deterioration must be checked, particularly where an essential metal component could be attacked.

The retro-reflecting device, or the whole lamp if the device is combined with a light, must have its removable parts removed. It must then withstand saline mist for 50 hours, as two 24-hour exposures separated by a 2-hour drying interval.
The saline mist must be produced by atomizing, at 35 °C ± 2 °C, a solution of 20 ± 2 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 80 parts of distilled water with no more than 0.02% impurities.
Immediately after the salt-mist test, the sample must not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.

The outer surface of the retro-reflecting device, especially the illuminating surface, must be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in 70 vol.% n-heptane and 30 vol.% toluol. After about five minutes it must show no apparent surface changes. Slight surface cracks are tolerated.

The outer surface of the retro-reflecting device, especially the illuminating surface, must be lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in detergent lubricating oil. After about 5 minutes it must be cleaned, and the CIL must then be measured as specified (Annex 4 para 3.2 or Annex 14 para 4.2).
The retro-reflecting device must be kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at 65 ±2°C as the heat-resistance test.
After the heat test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflecting device, and in particular of its optical component, may be visible.

The retro-reflecting device samples must be tested in the specified chronological order: visual inspection, shape and dimensions, heat, colorimetry, photometry, water, fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability in time and colour-fastness.
Mechanical and geometric conformity of production retro-reflectors is satisfied only if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the Regulation's requirements.
For any randomly chosen production retro-reflector, no measured photometric value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in the Regulation.
The chromaticity coordinates of production retro-reflectors shall be complied with.
The manufacturer's conformity tests shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the resistance to penetration of water.
Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
If the manufacturer uses equivalent methods in conformity tests, it needs the competent authority's consent and must prove the methods are equivalent to those in the Regulation.
Test apparatus used for CoP checks of the retro-reflector must be regularly calibrated and correlated with the competent authority's measurements.
In all cases the reference methods are those of UN R3, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
CoP samples of retro-reflectors must be selected at random from a uniform batch of the same type.
Sampled retro-reflectors must be measured photometrically at the points and for the chromaticity coordinates specified in the Regulation.

The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of the test results. With the competent authority, the manufacturer must define acceptability criteria that give at least 0.95 probability of passing a spot check at a 95% confidence level.
On inspector sampling, no measured photometric value of a randomly chosen retro-reflector may deviate unfavourably by more than 20% from the prescribed minimum values.
Retro-reflectors with apparent defects are disregarded in sampling.
The chromaticity coordinates must be complied with.
At first sampling, four retro-reflectors are selected at random and split into samples A and B.

Conformity is not contested if no specimen of A and B deviates by more than 20%. If it does deviate by more, the manufacturer must align production and a repeated sampling must follow within two months of notification.
At the first repeated sampling (samples C and D), conformity is not contested if no specimen deviates by more than 20%.

If one specimen of C or D deviates by more than 20% but none by more than 30%, the manufacturer must bring production into line again. A second repeated sampling must follow within two months of notification.
If a specimen of C or D deviates by more than 30%, approval is withdrawn under paragraph 9.
At the second repeated sampling (E and F), conformity is not contested if no specimen deviates by more than 20%. Otherwise approval is withdrawn.

One retro-reflector of sample A must be tested for resistance to penetration of water per Annex 8 para 1 (or Annex 14 para 3 for class IVA) and must pass. If it fails, both retro-reflectors of sample B must be tested and both must pass.

After each Annex 3 impact test, the lighting and signalling devices must continue to operate correctly and remain visible. Adjustment disturbed by the impact may be corrected only by the normal means of adjustment, and bulbs may be replaced only in the event of filament failure.

Fit the lighting and light-signalling devices so that, under normal conditions of use and despite vibrations, they retain the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation and enable the vehicle to comply. The lamps must not be capable of being inadvertently maladjusted.
When fitted to the vehicle, the reference axis of the lamp must be parallel to the road bearing plane, with a ±3° tolerance.
The reference axis must be parallel to the median longitudinal plane for signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, with a ±3° tolerance in each direction.
Any specific fitting instructions laid down by the manufacturer must be complied with.

Absent specific instructions, lamp height and orientation must be verified with the vehicle unladen on a flat horizontal surface, in the conditions of 2.3.10 to 2.3.10.2, with any AFS in its neutral state.
Absent specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair must be fitted symmetrically about the median longitudinal plane, judged on the exterior geometrical form of the lamp.
Lamps constituting a pair must be symmetrical to one another about the median longitudinal plane. This does not apply to the interior structure of the lamp.
Lamps constituting a pair must satisfy the same colorimetric requirements.
Lamps constituting a pair must have substantially identical photometric characteristics. This does not apply to a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.

Grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps are permitted only if all requirements for colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and any others are fulfilled.

Each lamp's photometric and colorimetric requirements must be fulfilled with all other grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated functions switched OFF. If a rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with functions that can be ON together with it, those functions' colour requirements must be met with both ON.
Measure maximum height above the ground from the highest point, and minimum height from the lowest point, of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis.

Width position is determined from the edge of the apparent surface (in the direction of the reference axis) furthest from the median longitudinal plane for overall width. For distance between lamps, it is determined from the inner edges. Exact edges need not be determined where compliance is clear.
Unless specific instructions allow it, the photometric characteristics (intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp must not be intentionally varied while the lamp is ON.

Any permitted variation in photometric characteristics (due to ambient light, other lamps switched ON/OFF, or the lamp providing another function) must comply with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle must not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

With the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, the apparent surface of a red lamp must not be directly visible towards the front to an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane 25 m in front of the vehicle (Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement is deemed fulfilled if the red light emitted to the front, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp, taking vehicle body influence into account if applicable. The white-to-rear part of the clause does not apply to this product's reversing lamp.

The electrical connections must be such that the rear position lamps can be switched ON and OFF only simultaneously with the front position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps and side-marker lamps (if they exist) and the rear registration plate lamp.
The rear lamp functions (rear position, stop, reversing) must not be concealable. Only main-beam, dipped-beam and front fog lamps may be concealed when not in use.
Light colours must match the table. The rear position lamp is red, the stop lamp is red, the reversing lamp is white, and the rear retro-reflector (triangular or non-triangular) is red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle for each function must equal the number indicated in the individual specifications of this Regulation.
Except for retro-reflectors, the lamp must be able to operate by the sole installation of a light source and/or a fuse. Otherwise it is deemed not present, even with an approval mark.

For M/N category vehicles, the applicant shall demonstrate to the Technical Service that the electric power supply conditions for the stop lamp and rear position lamp (and other listed devices) comply with the provisions of 5.27.x, with the vehicle electrical system in a representative constant-voltage condition.
A report describing the methods used to demonstrate compliance with the electric power supply provisions, and the results obtained, shall be attached to the approval documentation.

No obstacle may lie inside the geometric visibility angles to the propagation of light from any part of the lamp's apparent surface observed from infinity. Obstacles already present at lamp type approval are not counted.
If visibility measurements are taken closer than infinity, shift the direction of observation parallel to achieve the same accuracy.

If any part of the lamp's apparent surface is hidden by other vehicle parts when installed, proof shall be furnished that the unhidden part still meets the photometric values prescribed for approval of the device.
An LED module need not be replaceable only if this is stated in the communication sheet of the component type approval.

All lamps (devices), including the rear position, stop and reversing lamps and the retro-reflector where applicable, shall be type approved under the corresponding device Regulations specified in paragraph 6 when installed on a vehicle.
A reversing lamp must be present. It is mandatory on motor vehicles (and on trailers of categories O2, O3 and O4).
M1 vehicles must have one reversing lamp. A second reversing lamp is optional.
The reversing lamp devices must be type-approved to UN R23 (00 or subsequent series) or UN R148 (00 or subsequent series).
