The reversing lamp must be mounted not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground. The 1,400 mm maximum applies only to off-road N2G, N3G, M2G and M3G vehicles.
The reversing lamp must be positioned at the rear of the vehicle.

For a rear-mounted reversing lamp, geometric visibility must be α = 15° upwards and 5° downwards. For β, a single device needs 45° to the right and left. Two devices each need 45° outwards and 30° inwards.
The reversing lamp must be oriented rearwards.

The reversing lamp can be switched ON only if reverse gear is engaged and the propulsion start/stop control is in a position where propulsion operation is possible. It must not switch ON or remain ON if either condition is not met.
A tell-tale for the reversing lamp is optional. A failure tell-tale is mandatory only if the component regulation requires it.
Stop lamps of S1 or S2 category are mandatory on all vehicle categories, including M1. S3 or S4 devices are mandatory on M1 and N1, except for chassis-cabs and N1 vehicles with open cargo space.
Vehicle must have two S1 or S2 category stop lamps and one S3 or S4 category device. The devices must be type-approved to UN R7 (02 or later series) or UN R148 (00 or later series).

For M1/N1 vehicles, the S1/S2 stop lamp's apparent surface point farthest from the median longitudinal plane (in the direction of the reference axis) must be no more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

S1/S2 stop lamps must be mounted above the ground at not less than 350 mm and not more than 1,500 mm. The limit is 2,100 mm if the bodywork shape makes 1,500 mm impossible and the optional lamps are not installed.
S1/S2 stop lamps must be located at the rear of the vehicle.
S1/S2 stop lamps must be visible 45° to the left and right of the longitudinal axis. The inward angle may be reduced to 20° under the H plane for lamps mounted below 750 mm.

S1/S2 stop lamps must be visible 15° above and below the horizontal. The downward angle may be reduced to 5° if mounted below 750 mm. The upward angle may be reduced to 5° for optional lamps above 2,100 mm.
Stop lamp orientation must be towards the rear of the vehicle.
All stop lamps must be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
A tell-tale is optional. A tell-tale indicating failure is mandatory only if required by the component regulation.
Rear position lamps (devices of categories R, R1 or R2) are mandatory on the vehicle.
Fit two rear position lamps, type-approved to UN R7 (02 or subsequent series) or to UN R148 (00 or subsequent series).

The farthest point of the apparent surface must be no more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. This does not apply to optional lamps. For M1 there is no special requirement on the distance between the inner edges.

Mount the rear position lamp at a height above ground of at least 350 mm and no more than 1,500 mm. The limit may be 2,100 mm if bodywork makes 1,500 mm impossible and optional lamps are not installed.
Position the rear position lamp at the rear of the vehicle.

The rear position lamp must be visible within a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards, and a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal. The stated reductions apply only for mounting below 750 mm or, for optional lamps, above 2,100 mm.
The rear position lamp must be oriented rearwards.

The electrical connections of the rear position lamp must be in accordance with paragraph 5.11. The direction-indicator switch-off exception applies only if the lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a direction-indicator.

A closed-circuit tell-tale is mandatory for the rear position lamp and must be combined with that of the front position lamps. It is not required when daytime running lamps are switched ON. A failure tell-tale is mandatory if the component Regulation requires it.
A non-triangular rear retro-reflector must be fitted on motor vehicles (mandatory).

Two rear retro-reflectors are required, type-approved as Class IA or IB under UN R3 (02 or later series) or under UN R150 (00 or later series). Additional retro-reflecting devices are permitted if they do not impair the mandatory lighting and signalling devices.

The point on the retro-reflector's illuminating surface farthest from the median longitudinal plane must be no more than 400 mm from the vehicle's extreme outer edge. For M1 there is no special requirement for the distance between inner edges.

The retro-reflector height above ground must be at least 250 mm and at most 900 mm. The limit is 1,200 mm if grouped with rear lamp(s), or 1,500 mm if bodywork shape makes the lower limits impossible.
The rear retro-reflector must be positioned at the rear of the vehicle (length position).

The retro-reflector must be visible within 30° inwards and outwards horizontally and 10° above and below horizontal. The downward angle may be reduced to 5° if the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm.
The rear retro-reflector must be oriented rearwards.
The retro-reflector's illuminating surface may have parts in common with the apparent surface of any other lamp at the rear. This is a permission, not a mandatory requirement.

When DRLs are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON. They may be switched OFF, and remain OFF, only while ambient light outside the vehicle is above 7,000 lux (measured per Annex 13).

The emergency stop signal, mandatory on motor vehicles, shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7. The stop lamp in the rear lamp must be able to take part in that signal.
State in the approval communication whether a failure tell-tale, as required by the component regulation, is fitted for the rear position lamps (yes/no).
Declare in the approval communication whether rear retro-reflectors, non-triangular, are fitted (yes/no).

When checking visibility of the red lamp to the front, the observation zones are bounded in height by horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m above the ground. In width they are bounded by vertical planes at 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane.

Check the position of the lamps in width, height and length against the general requirements in paragraphs 2.10.2, 2.10.3, 2.10.4, 2.3.3 and 5.4. The measured distances must satisfy the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

Check the angles of geometric visibility per paragraph 2.10.7. The measured angles must meet each lamp's individual specifications. The limits may have an allowance for the ±3° mounting variation permitted in paragraph 5.3.
The electrical connections must be checked by switching on every lamp supplied by the vehicle's electrical system.
Lamps and tell-tales must function in accordance with paragraphs 5.11 to 5.14 of R48 and the individual specifications for each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, category of the lamps (including the rear position, stop and reversing functions) must be verifiable by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings. They must meet paragraphs 5.15 and 5.16 and the individual lamp specifications.
The application for approval must be submitted by the holder of the trade name or mark or by their duly accredited representative.
The application must state the purpose or purposes for which the device is intended and whether it may also be used in an assembly of two lamps of the same kind/type.
The application must state whether the device produces steady luminous intensity (R, R1, RM1, S1, S3) or variable luminous intensity (R2, RM2, S2, S4).

Supply drawings in triplicate, detailed enough to identify the device type. They must show the mounting geometry and reference axis and centre, the installation conditions that meet paragraph 6, any interdependent lamp combination, and the position of the approval mark.

Supply a brief technical description. Unless the lamp has non-replaceable light sources, it must state the prescribed LED light source category (UN R128) or the light source module identification code.
Submit two samples of the device. For symmetrical left/right devices, two identical samples for one side may be submitted.
The lamp must bear the applicant's trade name or mark, clearly legible and indelible.
The lamp must have a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the additional symbols under paragraph 4.2. This space must be shown in the drawings.

In a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, approval may be granted only if each lamp satisfies this Regulation or another Regulation. Lamps that don't satisfy any such Regulation cannot be part of the unit.

An approval number is assigned to each approved type. Its first two digits show the amendment series. The same Contracting Party shall not assign the same number to another type of device, except where approval is extended to a device differing only in colour of the light emitted.
Every device conforming to an approved type must bear an approval mark (per 4.2 and 4.3) in the space referred to in 3.3, in addition to the markings in 3.1 and 3.2 or 3.4.
The international approval mark must include a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country that granted approval.
The approval mark must include the approval number prescribed in 4.1.3.
Devices approved as rear position lamps must carry the letter "R", optionally followed by "1" for steady intensity or "2" for variable intensity, as an additional approval-mark symbol.
Devices approved as stop-lamps must carry the letter "S" followed by the figure 1, 2, 3 or 4. The figure depends on steady or variable intensity and on whether the S3 or S4 requirements are met.
Devices combining a rear position lamp and a stop lamp must be marked with "R", "R1" or "R2" and "S1" or "S2" as applicable, separated by a horizontal dash.
Approval marks and symbols must be clearly legible and indelible, even when the lamp is fitted in the vehicle.

For grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps that comply with several Regulations, a single international approval mark (circle with E, country number and approval number) may be affixed, subject to the visibility and light-transmitting-part conditions.
The single approval mark must be visible after installation.
No light-transmitting part of the combined lamp can be removed without also removing the approval mark.
Mark the identification symbol for each lamp under each Regulation of approval, with the series of amendments and the arrow if needed.
Place the identification symbols on the appropriate light-emitting surface (alternative to the group marking in 4.3.2.2.2).
Alternatively, mark the lamps as a group so that each grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamp can be clearly identified.
Each component of a single approval mark must be at least the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks.
Each approved type is assigned an approval number. The same Contracting Party may not assign that number to another type of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
The approval marking must be clearly legible and indelible.
The marking must be visible when the device is fitted on the vehicle, or when a movable part such as the hood, boot lid or a door is opened.

Meet the requirements of sections 5 and 6 and the referenced Annexes of UN R48, in the series in force at application. Apply the requirements pertinent to each lamp and vehicle category, where verification at lamp type approval is feasible.
Each device supplied must conform to the specifications in paragraphs 6 and 8 of R7.
The lamp must be designed and constructed so that, in normal use and despite vibrations, it keeps operating satisfactorily and keeps the characteristics prescribed by this Regulation.

The light from each of the two lamps supplied shall be, on the reference axis, not less than the minimum and not more than the maximum luminous intensity in the table. For rear position lamps this is min 4 cd and max 17 cd as a single lamp, or 8.5 cd if marked 'D'.

A rear position lamp of category R, R1 or RM1 (steady) shall meet the table's intensity limits on the reference axis: min 4 cd and max 17 cd. Category R2 or RM2 (variable) is limited to min 4 cd and max 42 cd.
The stop-lamp shall meet the table's min and max intensity on the reference axis for its category: S1 60–260 cd, S2 60–730 cd, S3 25–110 cd, S4 25–160 cd. 'D' lamps have lower maxima.
In a single lamp with more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that failure of any one makes all stop emitting light is considered one light source.

On failure of any one light source in a single multi-source lamp, either the Annex 4 minimum intensity is still met, or a failure tell-tale signal is produced. The tell-tale option requires at least 50% of the minimum intensity on the reference axis and a note in the communication form.
Outside the reference axis and within the Annex 1 angular fields, the intensity of each device supplied must meet the requirements of the subparagraphs.
In each Annex 4 table direction, intensity must be at least the paragraph 6.1 minimum multiplied by the table percentage for that direction.
In no direction within the visibility space may intensity exceed the maximum specified in the paragraph 6.1 table.
Throughout the Annex 1 fields, luminous intensity of a rear position lamp must be at least 0.05 cd.
The Annex 4 paragraph 2.2 provisions on local variations of intensity must be observed.
Intensities are measured with the light source(s) continuously alight. For red-emitting devices, measure in coloured light.
Use the measurement methods given in Annex 4, referred to in paragraph 6.2.1, for the photometric measurements.
Make all photometric and colorimetric measurements under the supply conditions of 7.1.1 to 7.1.4.
Record the voltage to be applied to the lamp in the Annex 2 communication form.
Determine the limits of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of the light-signalling device.

Light emitted inside the Annex 4 light distribution grid field must be red or white, with no sharp colour variation outside it. Verify colour with the paragraph 7 test procedure, and for non-replaceable light sources use the sources present in the lamp.
Conformity of production procedures must comply with those in the Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3), and the requirements that follow.
Manufacture lamps to conform to the approved type, and verify compliance with paragraphs 6 and 8.
Comply with the minimum conformity of production control procedure requirements in Annex 5.
Comply with the minimum requirements for sampling by an inspector in Annex 6.
If the approval holder completely ceases to manufacture a device approved under this Regulation, the holder must inform the authority that granted the approval.

The rear position lamp and stop lamp must give light distribution in space with minimum vertical angles of 15° above and 15° below the horizontal. The exceptions are mounting height under 750 mm (15° above, 5° below), optional lamps mounted above 2,100 mm (5° above, 15° below), and category S3/S4 stop lamps (10° above, 5° below). The horizontal angles follow the Annex 1 diagrams.
The communication for the lamp type must state the manufacturer's name and address.
If applicable, the communication must give the name and address of the manufacturer's representative.
The communication must state the date the lamp type was submitted for approval.
The communication must identify the Technical Service responsible for conducting the approval tests.
The communication must state the date of the report issued by the Technical Service.
The communication must state the number of the report issued by the Technical Service.

The communication must describe the lamp by category: mounting, colour of light, number, category and kind of light source(s), voltage and wattage, light source module identification code, limited mounting height, installation geometry, electronic control gear or variable intensity, and tell-tale use.
The communication must state the position of the approval mark.
The communication must state whether approval is granted, extended, refused or withdrawn.

On a combined rear position/stop lamp, place the approval number and additional symbols close to the circle and either above or below the letter "E", or to its right or left. The digits of the approval number must be on the same side of the E and face the same direction.

Where two or more lamps are part of the same assembly (grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated), the assembly may carry the simplified approval marking shown in the examples. The R7 functions in the housing are the rear position lamp and the stop lamp.
During photometric measurements, avoid stray reflections by appropriate masking.
If measurements are challenged, the measurement distance must be such that the inverse square law of distance applies.
If measurements are challenged, the receiver's angular aperture, viewed from the lamp's reference centre, must be between 10 angular minutes and one degree.
If measurements are challenged, an intensity requirement for a direction is deemed met if it is met in a direction deviating by no more than one-quarter of a degree.

Minimum intensities in the grid directions are expressed as a percentage of the minimum required on the reference axis (H=0°, V=0°). The reference axis is horizontal and parallel to the median longitudinal plane, and it passes through the centre of reference.
Within the grid field the light pattern must be substantially uniform. The intensity in each direction must meet at least the lowest minimum value on the surrounding grid lines.
For non-replaceable light sources, photometric performance is checked with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant sub-paragraph of paragraph 7.1.
For a signalling lamp without filament light sources, the luminous intensities measured after one minute and after 30 minutes of operation must comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
Conformity of production is satisfied mechanically and geometrically if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of the Regulation.
Conformity of mass-produced lamps on photometric performance (paragraph 6) is judged by testing randomly chosen lamps per paragraph 7. The sub-clauses give the deviation limits.

In production checks, no measured photometric value may deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the prescribed values. For minimum values the table gives the equivalent cd deviations (0.3 cd -> 0.1 cd; 0.05 cd -> 0.02 cd).
Colorimetric performance of production lamps must comply with paragraph 8 of the Regulation.

For each lamp type, the approval holder must carry out at least the specified tests at appropriate intervals in accordance with the Regulation. If sampling shows non-conformity, further samples must be taken and tested, and steps taken to ensure production conformity.
Manufacturer conformity tests must cover photometric and colorimetric characteristics.
Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.
Equivalent test methods may be used in manufacturer conformity tests only with the competent authority's consent. The manufacturer must prove the methods are equivalent to those in the Regulation.
Test apparatus used for conformity-of-production testing must be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
The reference methods in all cases are those of this Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
Samples of lamps must be selected at random from a uniform batch of the same type. Records from several factories may be grouped only if they operate under the same quality system and management.
Sampled lamps must be photometrically measured for the minimum values at the Annex 4 points and for the required chromaticity coordinates.

The manufacturer must carry out a statistical study of test results and define acceptability criteria in agreement with the competent authority. At 95% confidence, the minimum probability of passing an Annex 6 first-sampling spot check must be 0.95.
Conformity is considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
Conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if, when tested per paragraph 7, a randomly chosen lamp meets the photometric performance of paragraph 6 and the sub-paragraph criteria.
A randomly chosen production lamp must meet the requirements referred to in paragraph 1.2.1 of Annex 5 for conformity not to be contested.
Lamps with apparent defects are disregarded in the inspector's conformity sampling.
Chromaticity coordinates must comply when tested under the conditions of paragraph 7 of the Regulation (checked during CoP sampling).
In the first CoP sampling, four lamps are selected at random. Two are marked A and two are marked B.

Conformity of mass-produced lamps is not contested if no specimen of samples A and B (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20%. The measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample A deviate by not more than 0% (as printed in the clause).

If any specimen of A or B deviates by more than 20%, conformity is contested. The manufacturer must align production, repeat sampling takes place within two months of notification, and samples A and B are retained by the Technical Service until the CoP process is finished.
For the first repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment. Two are marked C and two are marked D.

Conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples C and D (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20%. The measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample C deviate by not more than 0% (as printed in the clause).

If one specimen of C or D deviates by more than 20% but none by more than 30%, the manufacturer must realign production. A second repeated sampling is carried out within two months of notification, and samples C and D are retained by the Technical Service until the CoP process is finished.
If any specimen of C or D deviates by more than 30%, the approval is withdrawn and paragraph 5 of Annex 6 applies.
For the second repeated sampling, four lamps are selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment. Two are marked E and two are marked F.

Conformity is not contested if no specimen of samples E and F (all four lamps) deviates by more than 20%. The measurement can be closed if both lamps of sample E deviate by not more than 0% (as printed in the clause).
If any specimen of E or F deviates by more than 20%, conformity is contested, the approval is withdrawn, and paragraph 5 of Annex 6 applies.
If conformity of production is contested in the Annex 6 sampling, the type approval is withdrawn according to paragraph 10 of UN R7.
